# Istor

> Istor is a free, open research notebook for Windows that runs entirely on your own machine. Add sources, ask grounded questions, and read answers where every claim carries a citation back to the passage it came from. Retrieval, prompting and inference happen locally, so a GTX 1650 class GPU is enough hardware and nothing leaves your computer unless you trigger a web fetch yourself.

The site at [istor.fyi](https://istor.fyi/) is the product's home page. It is static, makes zero network requests at runtime, and works without JavaScript.

## Pages

- [Home](https://istor.fyi/): what Istor is, how the research loop works, hardware and privacy facts, and the full FAQ.
- [Istor and NotebookLM, compared](https://istor.fyi/vs-notebooklm/): a factual comparison for people weighing a cloud notebook against one that runs on their own machine.
- [Istor and ChatGPT, compared](https://istor.fyi/vs-chatgpt/): a general-purpose cloud assistant with frontier-scale models, and a local research notebook where documents never leave your machine.
- [Istor and AnythingLLM, compared](https://istor.fyi/vs-anythingllm/): two open-source tools that run AI on your own documents locally, and the different bets they make.
- [Istor and GPT4All, compared](https://istor.fyi/vs-gpt4all/): one built to chat on any CPU, one built to ground research answers on a modest GPU.
- [Istor and Zotero, compared](https://istor.fyi/vs-zotero/): a reference manager organizes what you have read; a grounded local notebook reads it with you. Why they complement each other.
- [Istor and Mendeley, compared](https://istor.fyi/vs-mendeley/): the same pairing from the Elsevier side of the reference-manager world, and what each tool's trust model means for your library.
- [Istor and Obsidian, compared](https://istor.fyi/vs-obsidian/): a plain-text knowledge base of notes you write, and a local research notebook that reads the sources themselves. Two local-first tools, different jobs.
- [Can a local AI do a literature review?](https://istor.fyi/local-ai-literature-review/): what a grounded local tool contributes to reviewing literature, and where the line sits.
- [Local AI for field research](https://istor.fyi/local-ai-field-research/): the whole analysis loop offline, where ethics rules forbid uploads and coverage is unreliable.
- [Writing with sources, on a local AI](https://istor.fyi/local-ai-writing-projects/): keeping the library searchable beside the draft, with citations as you write.
- [Can you run a research AI on a GTX 1650?](https://istor.fyi/run-research-ai-gtx-1650/): what fits on entry-level GPU hardware and how the grounding loop runs on it.
- [Is local RAG private?](https://istor.fyi/is-local-rag-private/): what actually leaves the machine in a local retrieval loop, and the questions to ask of any tool.
- [What is retrieval-augmented generation?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-rag/): the technique behind chat with your documents, what it fixes, what it does not, and how it runs locally.
- [What is a local LLM?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-a-local-llm/): a language model that runs on your own hardware, what it can and cannot do, and what it takes to run one.
- [Does local AI need a GPU?](https://istor.fyi/does-local-ai-need-a-gpu/): no, small models run on a plain CPU, just slower; what a GPU buys and where research work wants even an entry-level card.
- [Can an AI do research with no internet?](https://istor.fyi/research-ai-offline/): what a local research AI does with the network unplugged, what it honestly cannot, and when offline is the point.
- [What is the most private way to chat with PDFs?](https://istor.fyi/private-pdf-chat/): a checklist for private document question answering, and how Istor satisfies each item.
- [Can a local AI read scanned PDFs?](https://istor.fyi/local-ai-scanned-pdfs/): local OCR and vision models read scans on your machine, and the limits of what photographs of pages give up.
- [What formats can a local AI read?](https://istor.fyi/what-formats-can-local-ai-read/): the common research formats read on your machine, and why a tool's format list is also its upload list.
- [Can a local AI summarize PDFs?](https://istor.fyi/can-local-ai-summarize-pdfs/): yes, on your machine; what makes a summary checkable, how long documents get handled, and where length limits bite.
- [Why do AI chatbots invent citations?](https://istor.fyi/why-ai-hallucinates-citations/): why language models generate plausible-looking references, why retrieval alone does not fix it, and what a verification gate does.
- [What is a context window?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-a-context-window/): the model's working memory, what fits inside it, and how retrieval decides what goes in.
- [What is an embedding?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-an-embedding/): the number representation that lets search match by meaning, and why the conversion runs fine locally.
- [What is quantization?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-quantization/): storing a model's numbers in fewer bits, the compression that lets serious models run on ordinary hardware.
- [What is tokenization?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-tokenization/): how text becomes the pieces a model reads, and why every limit is measured in tokens.
- [What is OCR?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-ocr/): reading text out of images of pages, where it fails, and why the conversion can stay on your machine.
- [Can a local AI translate documents?](https://istor.fyi/can-local-ai-translate-documents/): yes, translation is a core language task; what quality depends on and why the document never has to leave the disk.
- [How much RAM does a local AI need?](https://istor.fyi/how-much-ram-for-local-ai/): a quantized 7B model fits in about 5 gigabytes, so 16 GB is a comfortable setup; the model is the consumer, the library barely counts.
- [How does document chunking work?](https://istor.fyi/how-document-chunking-works/): why long documents are cut into passages before search, what good boundaries preserve, and why the step runs locally.
- [What is inference?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-inference/): running a trained model on your input to produce an answer; the act is offline, local, and changes nothing in the model.
- [What is a vector database?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-a-vector-database/): the index that matches meaning instead of wording, why a personal library needs no server product, and what the vectors point back to.
- [How do you stop an AI from making things up?](https://istor.fyi/how-to-stop-ai-hallucinating/): grounded retrieval, citations that open passages, a verification gate that refuses; confidence is not a fix, structure is.
- [What does 7B mean in a model name?](https://istor.fyi/what-does-7b-mean/): seven billion parameters, the learned numbers that carry everything a model knows; why the count sets the memory bill and 7B to 8B is the consumer sweet spot.
- [What is a GGUF file?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-a-gguf/): the single-file format local models ship in, weights plus metadata with quantization baked in; why it became the standard for local runtimes.
- [What is hybrid search?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-hybrid-search/): keyword search and vector search run together, each covering what the other misses; the merge that feeds retrieval, and why it runs on a laptop.
- [How do you cite an AI answer?](https://istor.fyi/how-to-cite-ai/): credit the tool in the text, cite the recoverable sources you verified, and disclose what you asked; the principles that outlast the style guides' current rules.
- [What is an open-weight model?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-open-weight/): a model whose trained numbers are downloadable, the completeness that makes local AI a copy operation; what open weights give you and what they still do not.
- [What is AI hallucination?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-ai-hallucination/): fluent, confident output with no basis in fact; why the same mechanism that makes models fluent makes them fabricate, and why the fixes are structural.
- [Can a local AI read handwriting?](https://istor.fyi/can-local-ai-read-handwriting/): neat handwriting mostly yes, hurried cursive with real limits; what local OCR and vision models manage on your machine and where checking stays essential.
- [What is fine-tuning?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-fine-tuning/): continuing a model's training to change behavior; why knowledge wants retrieval instead, and how LoRA made adaptation practical on ordinary hardware.
- [What is temperature in AI?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-temperature/): the setting that shapes how strictly a model sticks to its likeliest next words; low for facts, higher for drafts, and why it is not a creativity switch.
- [What is a system prompt?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-a-system-prompt/): the standing instructions a model reads before your first message; how it shapes behavior without adding knowledge, and why structure beats wording alone.
- [What is a model card?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-a-model-card/): the spec sheet that travels with a model; what to read first before you download, and why a card is a description with an interest rather than an audit.
- [What is tokens per second?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-tokens-per-second/): the rate a model writes, one token at a time; the reading-speed bar that makes local AI feel instant, and why speed says nothing about correctness.
- [Local AI for lecture notes](https://istor.fyi/local-ai-lecture-notes/): a semester's slides, readings and notes as one searchable library that answers with citations; what the tool keeps track of, and what stays yours to learn.
- [What is semantic search?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-semantic-search/): finding passages by meaning rather than wording, the retrieval step that makes a document library answerable; approximate by nature, which is why verification follows it.
- [What does Q4_K_M mean?](https://istor.fyi/what-does-q4-k-m-mean/): the code on a quantized model file naming its compression recipe; how to read the bits-per-weight headline, why K-series mixing protects quality, and which variant to pick.
- [What is prompt engineering?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-prompt-engineering/): writing instructions a model follows well; the unglamorous core that works, what words control and what they do not, and where structure takes over.
- [What is a vision language model?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-a-vision-language-model/): a language model that can also look at images; how it reads page photographs directly, what it keeps that plain OCR throws away, and why its reading still needs checking.
- [Why is local AI slow on my laptop?](https://istor.fyi/why-is-local-ai-slow-on-my-laptop/): model size, memory bandwidth, and one-token-at-a-time generation; what actually speeds a local model up, what does nothing, and why slow never makes answers worse.
- [What is training data?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-training-data/): the text a model learns from; why the model carries compressed tendencies rather than copies, and why knowledge wants a retrievable library instead of weights.
- [Can a local AI read spreadsheets?](https://istor.fyi/can-local-ai-read-spreadsheets/): yes, with caveats; CSV reads as plain text, Excel needs its cells extracted first, layout rarely survives, and model arithmetic wants checking.
- [Why does AI forget the beginning of long documents?](https://istor.fyi/why-does-ai-forget-the-beginning-of-long-documents/): one reading, uneven attention; why details near the start and middle get less weight in long inputs, and why retrieval beats a bigger window.
- [What is llama.cpp?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-llama-cpp/): the open-source engine under most local AI; how it runs GGUF models on CPUs and GPUs alike, and why it sits underneath so many tools.
- [What is model distillation?](https://istor.fyi/what-is-distillation/): training a small model on a larger one's outputs; how the student inherits the teacher's behavior at a fraction of the size, and what it loses.

## Download

Windows builds live at [github.com/ThoriaDevelopment/Istor/releases/latest](https://github.com/ThoriaDevelopment/Istor/releases/latest). The source is open under the repository's license.
